rows.note: This is the all-purpose everyday choice for dawn or daybreak, including the time around sunrise.

example.english: It's dawn, and we're heading to work.
example.jyutping: tin1 gwong1 laa3 ngo5 dei6 faan1 gung1 laa3

rows.note: Use this when you mean the exact event or time of the sun coming up rather than the surrounding dawn period.

example.english: At dawn, the whole sea turned golden.
example.traditional: 日出嗰陣，成個海面都變金色。
example.jyutping: jat6 ceot1 go2 zan6 seng4 go3 hoi2 min6 dou1 bin3 gam1 sik1

rows.note: Use this for the earliest phase of a development, such as the early period of civilization.

example.english: In the dawn of civilization, people didn't yet know how to use electricity.
example.traditional: 初期嘅文明，人哋仲未識用電。
example.jyutping: co1 kei4 ge3 man4 ming4 jan4 dei6 zung6 mei6 sik1 jung6 din6

rows.note: Use this more formal term when referring specifically to the twilight immediately before sunrise.

example.english: At dawn, the sky is still gray-blue.
example.traditional: 黎明時分，天空仲係一片灰藍。
example.jyutping: lai4 ming4 si4 fan1 tin1 hung1 zung6 hai6 jat1 pin3 fui1 laam4
